description: NSA PRISM documents leaked by Snowden in 2013 listed Facebook as a participating company giving the NSA direct access to user data since 2009; Zuckerberg denied knowing of the program
Google was listed as a PRISM participant in NSA documents leaked by Snowden, providing the NSA access to user emails, documents, and search queries; Google denied knowingly participating
Mark Zuckerberg was named a World Economic Forum Young Global Leader in 2009; he has been a regular Davos attendee and hosted WEF sessions on technology and connectivity

Epstein owned Zorro Ranch, a 10,000-acre compound in New Mexico where multiple victims say they were abused; the FBI investigated the property in 2019 and court documents allege sex trafficking occurred there

Maxwell founded the Terramar Project, a nonprofit ostensibly protecting oceans; critics and prosecutors have alleged it was used to facilitate international travel and provided a cover story for activities on Epstein's private island
Epstein owned Little Saint James, a private island in the US Virgin Islands where victims say he ran a sex-trafficking operation; the island was raided by the FBI after Epstein's 2019 arrest

The CIA Inspector General's 1998 report confirmed Oliver North's NSC operation coordinated with CIA officers to funnel arms and money to the Contras, bypassing Congress through a secret funding network

Philip Zelikow served as Executive Director of the 9/11 Commission despite having co-authored a book with Condoleezza Rice and serving on the Bush transition team — a conflict of interest that critics say shaped the final report

As FBI Director, Robert Mueller signed off on the 2008 non-prosecution agreement with Epstein; the sweetheart deal, brokered by Alex Acosta, gave Epstein immunity for federal crimes and was later ruled illegal

Alex Acosta, as US Attorney for South Florida, secretly negotiated a 2008 non-prosecution agreement with Epstein's lawyers giving him only 13 months in a work-release program; Acosta later resigned as Trump's Labor Secretary over the deal

Declassified documents confirm the CIA provided Saddam Hussein with intelligence on Iranian troop positions in the 1980s, knowing he was using chemical weapons against them; the US supported Iraq throughout the Iran-Iraq War

Wikileaks cables revealed the US State Department and CIA worked as 'de facto global ambassadors' for Monsanto, pressuring foreign governments to accept GMO crops and drop restrictions on Monsanto products

Soros's Open Society Foundations spent over $100 million in Ukraine since 1990 funding civil society groups; he backed the 2014 Maidan uprising and his foundation has co-financed Ukrainian government reform programs

A leaked phone call revealed US Assistant Secretary of State Victoria Nuland saying 'Fuck the EU' while discussing who should lead Ukraine's post-Maidan government in 2014, confirming US involvement in the political transition

Halliburton subsidiary KBR received no-bid contracts worth $39.5 billion in the Iraq War reconstruction effort; the company was awarded contracts before the invasion had even begun, by the Pentagon under Cheney
The CIA hired Blackwater (later Academi) for covert assassination missions and targeted killing programs in Pakistan and Afghanistan; CIA director Leon Panetta terminated one such program in 2009

Erik Prince, founder of Blackwater, ran a CIA-authorized assassination program and served as the CIA's 'asset' in Afghanistan and Pakistan according to the New York Times and Intercept; he later pitched a CIA-run private spy service

Peter Thiel donated $1.25 million to Trump's 2016 campaign and was the only major Silicon Valley figure to speak at the Republican National Convention; Thiel received a presidential pardon for a Palantir associate after the election

Cambridge Analytica, through its UK affiliate AggregateIQ, provided data-targeting services to the official Vote Leave campaign; the UK's Information Commissioner found the campaigns violated data protection laws

Many of the same individuals attend both Bilderberg and Davos, including Kissinger, David Rockefeller, and various heads of state; both forums exclude press and operate under Chatham House rules or total secrecy
Epstein's 2008 deal allowed him to secretly sign a non-prosecution agreement with US Attorney Alex Acosta that granted immunity not only to Epstein but also to any 'potential co-conspirators'

Obama received more money from Wall Street during the 2008 election than any previous presidential candidate — over $15 million from the financial sector — and then filled his administration with Goldman Sachs and Citigroup alumni

Multiple former Monsanto executives and lawyers have cycled through the FDA in senior regulatory roles — a 'revolving door' pattern including Michael Taylor, who drafted FDA's GMO policy and later returned to Monsanto as VP

The CIA oversaw the largest covert operation in its history by arming Mujahideen fighters in Afghanistan through Operation Cyclone; a 1989 report by the CIA's own inspector general admitted the program helped create the conditions for the Taliban

Bin Laden, working through Pakistan's ISI, received CIA-funneled weapons and funding as a Mujahideen commander during the Soviet-Afghan War; the CIA's connection was documented in the 9/11 Commission Report

Roger Stone has been Trump's political adviser and friend since the 1980s; Stone was convicted of seven felony counts including witness tampering and lying to Congress and was pardoned by Trump in December 2020

Virginia Giuffre accused Alan Dershowitz of sexually abusing her when she was underage while she was trafficked by Epstein; Dershowitz has vigorously denied the allegations and sued the lawyers who published them

The FDA receives 65% of its drug review budget from 'user fees' paid by pharmaceutical companies including Pfizer; critics argue this creates a structural conflict of interest in drug approval decisions

On his last day in office, Clinton pardoned fugitive financier Marc Rich, who had fled the US to avoid prosecution for tax evasion and illegal oil deals with Iran; Rich's ex-wife Denise had donated $450,000 to the Clinton Library

Fauci served as a key US representative to the WHO for decades, coordinating pandemic responses; he was among the WHO advisers who in January 2020 praised China's transparency on COVID-19, which critics said delayed the global response

Musk acquired Twitter for $44 billion in 2022, renaming it X; he used $13 billion in debt financing from Morgan Stanley and others while cutting 80% of staff, dramatically reshaping global information flows

Julian Assange founded WikiLeaks in 2006 and served as its editor-in-chief; the site published millions of classified US military and diplomatic documents including the 'Collateral Murder' video of a 2007 Baghdad airstrike

The CIA under Mike Pompeo designated WikiLeaks a 'non-state hostile intelligence service' in 2017 and drew up plans to kidnap or assassinate Assange in the Ecuadorian Embassy; Yahoo News reported this in 2021

Rumsfeld was CEO of G.D. Searle when it developed aspartame; after FDA reviewers rejected it, Rumsfeld joined the Reagan transition team and the next day Reagan appointed an FDA commissioner who approved aspartame in 1981

The Gates Foundation has funded the ID2020 Alliance and similar digital identity programs in developing nations, raising concerns from civil libertarians about biometric surveillance infrastructure in aid-dependent countries

Musk co-founded Neuralink in 2016 to develop brain-computer implants; the company received DARPA-adjacent funding and is developing technology that would allow direct neural interfaces with AI systems

Klaus Schwab co-authored 'COVID-19: The Great Reset' in July 2020, calling for governments to use the pandemic to 'revamp all aspects of our societies and economies'; the book became central to conspiracy theories about elite pandemic exploitation

Hunter Biden was paid up to $83,333 per month to sit on the board of Ukrainian gas company Burisma Holdings between 2014 and 2019, while his father Joe Biden was VP and the lead US official on Ukraine policy

Biden, as VP, boasted in a 2018 Council on Foreign Relations speech that he threatened to withhold $1 billion in US loan guarantees unless Ukraine fired prosecutor Viktor Shokin — who was investigating Burisma while Hunter was on its board

Epstein's associate and Virgin Islands financial contacts overlapped with sovereign wealth and asset management networks; Epstein's estate held accounts at Deutsche Bank, which was later fined $150 million for processing his transactions

Deutsche Bank was fined $150 million by New York State regulators in 2020 for processing $120 million in suspicious transactions for Jeffrey Epstein between 2013 and 2019, despite his sex-offender status being public

The CIA's founding director Allen Dulles and key figures including Zbigniew Brzezinski and George H.W. Bush held senior CFR positions; historians document a decades-long overlap between CFR membership and senior CIA leadership
Virginia Giuffre has testified under oath that Epstein and Maxwell trafficked her to powerful men beginning when she was 17; she named Prince Andrew, Alan Dershowitz, and others in legal proceedings

Snowden documents revealed that the NSA and Britain's GCHQ jointly ran mass surveillance programs including MUSCULAR, tapping fiber-optic cables to intercept data from Google and Yahoo data centers without warrants

Bill Clinton attended the 1991 Bilderberg meeting in Baden-Baden, Germany while still Arkansas Governor; the following year he won the Democratic nomination and the presidency — mirroring the pattern of earlier Bilderberg-endorsed candidates

The WEF launched the 'Great Reset' initiative in June 2020, with Schwab and Prince Charles as co-chairs; it called for a fundamental transformation of capitalism using COVID-19 as an opportunity to rebuild economies sustainably

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund invested $2 billion in Kushner's private equity firm Affinity Partners in 2022, just 6 months after Kushner left his White House role where he had been the lead on Saudi relations

Jared Kushner is the son-in-law of Donald Trump, having married Trump's daughter Ivanka in 2009; Kushner served as Senior Adviser to the President with an expansive portfolio covering Middle East policy and federal reform

Bill Gates became the largest private owner of US farmland by 2021, with over 269,000 acres across 18 states; this concentration of agricultural land ownership has raised concerns about food system control

Soros has donated over $131 million to media organizations since 2003, including NPR, ProPublica, the Guardian, and hundreds of local newspapers, according to a Media Research Center analysis of Open Society grants

Declassified documents confirm the Tavistock Institute of Human Relations received CIA funding through front foundations in the 1950s; Tavistock researchers developed psychological influence and mind-control frameworks later adopted by intelligence agencies
